1	import type { ObjectCurrentVertexTypes } from '@traversable-object-tree/lib/ObjectCurrentVertexTypes';
2	import {
3	  assertOwnKeys,
4	  assertOptionalCallbacks,
5	  TREE_OPTION_KEYS,
6	  OBJECT_SOURCE_OPTION_KEYS,
7	  OBJECT_MUTATION_OPTION_KEYS,
8	  definedOptions,
9	} from '@core/assertPublicOptions';
10	import type { GetPathToOptions } from '@core/ResolvedTree';
11	import { TraversalRunnerStatus } from '@core/TraversalRunner';
12	import type { TreeVisitorContext } from '@core/TraversalVisitor';
13	import type { VertexView } from '@core/Vertex';
14	import type { DepthFirstTreeOptionsPatch } from '@depth-first-traversal/lib/DepthFirstTraversalInstanceConfig';
15	import { DepthFirstPhase } from '@depth-first-traversal/lib/DepthFirstTraversalOrder';
16	import type { DepthFirstTreeRunner } from '@depth-first-traversal/lib/DepthFirstTraversalRunner';
17	import { DepthFirstTreeTraversal } from '@depth-first-traversal/DepthFirstTraversal';
18	import type {
19	  ObjectMutationOptions,
20	  ObjectMutationRequest,
21	} from '@traversable-object-tree/lib/makeMutationCommandFactory';
22	import type { ObjectCompositeClassification } from '@traversable-object-tree/lib/TO_IsCompositeAssertionsMixin';
23	import type { TraversableObject } from '@traversable-object-tree/lib/TraversableObject';
24	import type { TraversableObjectPropKey } from '@traversable-object-tree/lib/TraversableObjectPropKey';
25	import type {
26	  ObjectTreeOptions,
27	  ObjectTreeBaseOptions,
28	  ObjectTreePropertyAdapters,
29	} from '@traversable-object-tree/lib/TraversableObjectTreeInstanceConfig';
30	import type { ObjectTreeVertexTypes } from '@traversable-object-tree/lib/ObjectTreeVertexTypes';
31	import { ObjectTreeSource } from '@traversable-object-tree/TraversableObjectTree';
32	
33	export type ObjectRewriteContext<
34	  InK extends TraversableObjectPropKey,
35	  InV,
36	  OutK extends TraversableObjectPropKey,
37	  OutV,
38	> = TreeVisitorContext<
39	  DepthFirstPhase.POST_ORDER,
40	  ObjectTreeVertexTypes<InK, InV>,
41	  ObjectCurrentVertexTypes<
42	    ObjectTreeVertexTypes<InK, InV>,
43	    ObjectTreeVertexTypes<OutK, OutV>
44	  >
45	> &
46	  ObjectCompositeClassification & {
47	    vertex: VertexView<
48	      ObjectCurrentVertexTypes<
49	        ObjectTreeVertexTypes<InK, InV>,
50	        ObjectTreeVertexTypes<OutK, OutV>
51	      >
52	    >;
53	    getKeyPath: (options?: GetPathToOptions) => (InK | OutK)[];
54	  };
55	
56	export type ObjectRewriteInput<
57	  InK extends TraversableObjectPropKey,
58	  InV,
59	  OutK extends TraversableObjectPropKey,
60	  OutV,
61	> = ObjectCurrentVertexTypes<
62	  ObjectTreeVertexTypes<InK, InV>,
63	  ObjectTreeVertexTypes<OutK, OutV>
64	>['VertexData'] & {
65	  assembledComposite?: unknown;
66	};
67	
68	export type ObjectRewriteCallback<
69	  InK extends TraversableObjectPropKey,
70	  InV,
71	  OutK extends TraversableObjectPropKey,
72	  OutV,
73	> = (
74	  prop: ObjectRewriteInput<InK, InV, OutK, OutV>,
75	  context: ObjectRewriteContext<InK, InV, OutK, OutV>,
76	) => ObjectMutationRequest<ObjectTreeVertexTypes<OutK, OutV>> | undefined;
77	
78	export const __REWRITE_OBJECT_DEFAULT_ROOT_KEY__ =
79	  '__REWRITE_OBJECT_DEFAULT_ROOT_KEY__';
80	
81	/** Root presence is independent of a legitimate null/undefined converted value. */
82	export type ObjectRewriteOutputResult<Out> =
83	  | Readonly<{ kind: 'present'; value: Out }>
84	  | Readonly<{ kind: 'absent' }>;
85	
86	export type RewriteObjectResult<
87	  InK extends TraversableObjectPropKey,
88	  InV,
89	  Out,
90	  OutK extends TraversableObjectPropKey,
91	  OutV,
92	> = {
93	  /** Converted output captured at return, possibly partial before completion. */
94	  outputResultAtReturn: ObjectRewriteOutputResult<Out>;
95	  /** Final converted output; throws until the runner has finished. */
96	  getOutputResult(): ObjectRewriteOutputResult<Out>;
97	  traversalRunner: DepthFirstTreeRunner<
98	    ObjectTreeVertexTypes<InK, InV>,
99	    ObjectCurrentVertexTypes<
100	      ObjectTreeVertexTypes<InK, InV>,
101	      ObjectTreeVertexTypes<OutK, OutV>
102	    >
103	  >;
104	};
105	
106	export type RewriteObjectOptions<
107	  In,
108	  InK extends TraversableObjectPropKey,
109	  InV,
110	  Out,
111	  OutK extends TraversableObjectPropKey,
112	  OutV,
113	> = ObjectTreeOptions<In, InK, InV, OutK, OutV> &
114	  Partial<
115	    ObjectMutationOptions<
116	      ObjectTreeVertexTypes<InK, InV>,
117	      ObjectTreeVertexTypes<OutK, OutV>
118	    > &
119	      Omit<
120	        DepthFirstTreeOptionsPatch<
121	          ObjectTreeVertexTypes<InK, InV>,
122	          ObjectCurrentVertexTypes<
123	            ObjectTreeVertexTypes<InK, InV>,
124	            ObjectTreeVertexTypes<OutK, OutV>
125	          >
126	        >,
127	        'traversableTree'
128	      >
129	  > & {
130	    traversableTree?: never;
131	    rewrite?: ObjectRewriteCallback<InK, InV, OutK, OutV>;
132	    assembleCompositesBeforeRewrite?: boolean;
133	  } & (unknown extends Out
134	    ? { convertRootValue?: RootValueConverter<Out> }
135	    : { convertRootValue: RootValueConverter<Out> });
136	
137	export type RootValueConverter<Out> = (
138	  value: unknown,
139	  context: { readonly complete: boolean },
140	) => Out;
141	
142	export function rewriteObject<
143	  In = TraversableObject<TraversableObjectPropKey, unknown>,
144	  InK extends TraversableObjectPropKey = TraversableObjectPropKey,
145	  InV = unknown,
146	  Out = unknown,
147	  OutK extends TraversableObjectPropKey = InK,
148	  OutV = InV,
149	>(
150	  object: In,
151	  ...args: Record<never, never> extends RewriteObjectOptions<
152	    In,
153	    InK,
154	    InV,
155	    Out,
156	    OutK,
157	    OutV
158	  >
159	    ? [options?: RewriteObjectOptions<In, InK, InV, Out, OutK, OutV>]
160	    : [options: RewriteObjectOptions<In, InK, InV, Out, OutK, OutV>]
161	): RewriteObjectResult<InK, InV, Out, OutK, OutV> {
162	  const [inputOptions] = args;
163	  if (inputOptions !== undefined)
164	    assertOwnKeys(inputOptions, [
165	      ...TREE_OPTION_KEYS.filter((key) => key !== 'traversableTree'),
166	      ...OBJECT_SOURCE_OPTION_KEYS,
167	      ...OBJECT_MUTATION_OPTION_KEYS,
168	      'inOrder',
169	      'rewrite',
170	      'convertRootValue',
171	      'assembleCompositesBeforeRewrite',
172	    ]);
173	  const options =
174	    inputOptions === undefined ? undefined : definedOptions(inputOptions);
175	  if (options !== undefined) {
176	    assertOptionalCallbacks(options, [
177	      ...OBJECT_SOURCE_OPTION_KEYS,
178	      'isArray',
179	      'isObject',
180	      'assembleArray',
181	      'assembleObject',
182	      'rewrite',
183	      'convertRootValue',
184	    ]);
185	    if (
186	      options.assembleCompositesBeforeRewrite !== undefined &&
187	      typeof options.assembleCompositesBeforeRewrite !== 'boolean'
188	    )
189	      throw new TypeError('assembleCompositesBeforeRewrite must be boolean');
190	  }
191	  const assembleCompositeBeforeVisit =
192	    options?.assembleCompositesBeforeRewrite ?? false;
193	  const rewrite =
194	    typeof options?.rewrite === 'function' ? options.rewrite : null;
195	  const convertRootValue: RootValueConverter<Out> =
196	    options?.convertRootValue ?? ((value: unknown) => value as Out);
197	  const resolveChildHook = options?.resolveChildHook;
198	  // Required narrow adapters are enforced by RewriteObjectOptions. The default
199	  // mapper preserves the actual input; its discovery domain is broad.
200	  const tree = ObjectTreeSource.fromProperties<In, InK, InV, OutK, OutV>(
201	    object,
202	    {
203	      ...(resolveChildHook === undefined ? {} : { resolveChildHook }),
204	      getChildrenOfProperty:
205	        options?.getChildrenOfProperty ??
206	        ObjectTreeSource.getChildrenOfPropertyDefault,
207	      getRootPropertyFromInputObject:
208	        options?.getRootPropertyFromInputObject ??
209	        ObjectTreeSource.createRootPropertyMapper(
210	          __REWRITE_OBJECT_DEFAULT_ROOT_KEY__,
211	        ),
212	    } as ObjectTreeBaseOptions<In, InK, InV, OutK, OutV> &
213	      ObjectTreePropertyAdapters<In, InK, InV>,
214	  );
215	  const bindObjectMutation = ObjectTreeSource.createObjectMutationBinder<
216	    ObjectTreeVertexTypes<InK, InV>,
217	    ObjectTreeVertexTypes<OutK, OutV>
218	  >({
219	    ...(options?.arrayIndexPolicy === undefined
220	      ? {}
221	      : { arrayIndexPolicy: options.arrayIndexPolicy }),
222	    ...(options?.propertyCollision === undefined
223	      ? {}
224	      : { propertyCollision: options.propertyCollision }),
225	    ...(options?.isArray ? { isArray: options.isArray } : {}),
226	    ...(options?.isObject ? { isObject: options.isObject } : {}),
227	    ...(options?.assembleArray ? { assembleArray: options.assembleArray } : {}),
228	    ...(options?.assembleObject
229	      ? { assembleObject: options.assembleObject }
230	      : {}),
231	    ...(options?.assembledMap === undefined
232	      ? { assembledMap: new Map() }
233	      : { assembledMap: options.assembledMap }),
234	  });
235	  const traversal = new DepthFirstTreeTraversal<
236	    ObjectTreeVertexTypes<InK, InV>,
237	    ObjectCurrentVertexTypes<
238	      ObjectTreeVertexTypes<InK, InV>,
239	      ObjectTreeVertexTypes<OutK, OutV>
240	    >
241	  >({
242	    traversableTree: tree,
243	    ...{
244	      ...(options?.transformChildHints === undefined
245	        ? {}
246	        : { transformChildHints: options.transformChildHints }),
247	      ...(options?.visitors === undefined
248	        ? {}
249	        : { visitors: options.visitors }),
250	      ...(options?.inOrder === undefined ? {} : { inOrder: options.inOrder }),
251	      ...(options?.retainOriginalTreeStructure === undefined
252	        ? {}
253	        : {
254	            retainOriginalTreeStructure: options.retainOriginalTreeStructure,
255	          }),
256	    },
257	  });
258	  traversal.addVisitorFor(
259	    DepthFirstPhase.POST_ORDER,
260	    (
261	      vertex: VertexView<
262	        ObjectCurrentVertexTypes<
263	          ObjectTreeVertexTypes<InK, InV>,
264	          ObjectTreeVertexTypes<OutK, OutV>
265	        >
266	      >,
267	      context: TreeVisitorContext<
268	        DepthFirstPhase.POST_ORDER,
269	        ObjectTreeVertexTypes<InK, InV>,
270	        ObjectCurrentVertexTypes<
271	          ObjectTreeVertexTypes<InK, InV>,
272	          ObjectTreeVertexTypes<OutK, OutV>
273	        >
274	      >,
275	    ) => {
276	      const {
277	        makeMutationCommand,
278	        isComposite,
279	        isObject,
280	        isArray,
281	        assembleComposite,
282	      } = bindObjectMutation(vertex, context);
283	      let rwInput: ObjectRewriteInput<InK, InV, OutK, OutV> = vertex.getData();
284	      if (assembleCompositeBeforeVisit && isComposite) {
285	        rwInput = { ...rwInput, assembledComposite: assembleComposite() };
286	      }
287	      const rw = rewrite?.(rwInput, {
288	        ...context,
289	        isComposite,
290	        isObject,
291	        isArray,
292	        vertex,
293	        getKeyPath: (thisOptions?: GetPathToOptions) =>
294	          context.resolvedTreeView
295	            .requirePathTo(context.vertexRef, thisOptions)
296	            .map((ps) => ps.getValue().getData().key),
297	      });
298	      return { commands: [makeMutationCommand(rw)] };
299	    },
300	  );
301	  const traversalRunner = traversal.createRunner().run();
302	  const convertCurrentRoot = (): ObjectRewriteOutputResult<Out> => {
303	    const resolvedTreeView = traversalRunner.getResolvedTreeView();
304	    const rootRef = resolvedTreeView.getRoot();
305	    if (rootRef === null || !resolvedTreeView.has(rootRef)) {
306	      return Object.freeze({ kind: 'absent' });
307	    }
308	    return Object.freeze({
309	      kind: 'present',
310	      value: convertRootValue(rootRef.getValue().getData().value, {
311	        complete:
312	          traversalRunner.getStatus() === TraversalRunnerStatus.FINISHED,
313	      }),
314	    });
315	  };
316	  const outputResultAtReturn = convertCurrentRoot();
317	  let hasFinalOutput =
318	    traversalRunner.getStatus() === TraversalRunnerStatus.FINISHED;
319	  let finalOutput = outputResultAtReturn;
320	  return {
321	    outputResultAtReturn,
322	    traversalRunner,
323	    getOutputResult() {
324	      if (traversalRunner.getStatus() !== TraversalRunnerStatus.FINISHED) {
325	        throw new Error('Rewrite output is not complete');
326	      }
327	      if (!hasFinalOutput) {
328	        finalOutput = convertCurrentRoot();
329	        hasFinalOutput = true;
330	      }
331	      return finalOutput;
332	    },
333	  };
334	}
335	
336	/** Select an output type as a caller assertion, without runtime schema validation. */
337	export function rewriteObjectAs<Out>(
338	  object: unknown,
339	  options?: RewriteObjectOptions<
340	    unknown,
341	    TraversableObjectPropKey,
342	    unknown,
343	    unknown,
344	    TraversableObjectPropKey,
345	    unknown
346	  >,
347	): RewriteObjectResult<
348	  TraversableObjectPropKey,
349	  unknown,
350	  Out,
351	  TraversableObjectPropKey,
352	  unknown
353	> {
354	  // This helper is the explicit caller assertion. Ordinary rewriteObject keeps
355	  // the unknown result unless convertRootValue establishes a typed output.
356	  return rewriteObject(object, options) as RewriteObjectResult<
357	    TraversableObjectPropKey,
358	    unknown,
359	    Out,
360	    TraversableObjectPropKey,
361	    unknown
362	  >;
363	}

30	## Hint ownership
31	
32	Source content, standalone construction/clone patches and hint replacement commands accept readonly arrays. Vertex copies the membership array, including when cloned from another Vertex; editing the copy cannot change the original collection. Data and hint element objects retain shallow identity. Observed vertex collections remain frozen/detached. transformChildHints may invent, remove, duplicate or reorder hints; callers seeking sorting only should return a permutation themselves.
33	
34	## Limits and sessions
35	
36	replaceLimits replaces the entire previous limits record, rather than merging bounds. Include every bound you wish to retain; omitted/undefined replaceLimits retains the previous record. Validation is atomic, including route-mode bounds. Old limits patch keys reject even with own undefined. A constructor still takes limits.
37	
38	Binding two sessions to one runner shares progress but does not share ticket authority. A ticket belongs to its issuing wrapper. Use preparedDag.createWorkSession() for independent progress; its topology is shared, not its work state. Keep settlement generations and tickets local.
39	
40	## Presence and identity
41	
42	outputResultAtReturn and getOutputResult() return `{ kind: 'present', value }` or `{ kind: 'absent' }`. Switch on kind before reading value. A present null or undefined remains present. Converters run only for present roots, receive the existing complete flag, and never interpret deletion. The captured result stays fixed; the final getter requires FINISHED and caches its first successful result. Existing failed conversion values propagate exactly and can be retried.
43	
44	DAG omissions require explicit identity: null for anonymous, or `{ vertexId }` for known identity, including undefined/null/object/symbol IDs. During hint/prerequisite resolution, the requested identity can still supply an otherwise anonymous omission. Preserve satisfiesDependencies: true independently. Copy identity wrappers when converting records; never infer identity presence through truthiness. Structural result getters are supported; a known identity wrapper must contain an own vertexId. Raw top-level omitted.vertexId is rejected, and tree source results reject graph identity metadata.
45	
46	Milestone explanations now discriminate unresolved, deleted, live and omitted. Live progress is non-null; omitted progress is null and its milestone is satisfied. A deferred/ready vertex is live, not completed. Diagnostic wait edges still mean waiter waits for prerequisite. Structural component lists are SCC membership, never consecutive cycle edges; discovery witnesses remain ordered and closed.
47	
48	## Query and reconstruction choices
49	
50	Use has()/nullable sibling queries to check absent handles. requireVertexId, requirePathsTo and requirePathTo intentionally throw for absence; null/undefined are valid IDs and cannot serve as failure sentinels. isChildExpansionSkipped reports an explicit DFS skip, not a structural leaf. Use hasNoChildHints for hint emptiness and the resolved child view for structural children, considering incomplete discovery.
51	
52	liveVertexSummaries intentionally omits omission slots and entry metadata. Persist/revise/compose from definition, which preserves ordered slots, omissions and entry. mapDagFragmentIds maps caller identities explicitly; it does not issue a nominal instance capability. GraphWalkTarget and GraphWalkLink accept an optional trailing hydration mode to preserve mode-specific helper return types without assertions.
53	
54	## Source and callback vocabulary
55	
56	Only prerequisite lookup accepts `{ kind: 'missing' }`. All source resolutions use canonical tags; undefined and vertexContent:null legacy result forms are rejected. isArray/isObject are configuration predicates, while isComposite and getKeyPath are bound observations. Walking fromVertex identifies an endpoint; source config identifies the adapter. Callback timing, committed W/C observations, selector independence, resource disposal and package loader identity are unchanged.
57	
58	
59	## Tagged output example
60	
61	<!-- standalone -->
62	
63	```ts
64	import { rewriteObject } from 'configurable-tree-traversal';
65	
66	const retained = rewriteObject(null).getOutputResult();
67	if (retained.kind !== 'present' || retained.value !== null) {
68	  throw new Error('Expected a present null document');
69	}
70	const deleted = rewriteObject({ task: 1 }, {
71	  rewrite: () => ({ kind: 'delete' }),
72	}).getOutputResult();
73	if (deleted.kind !== 'absent') throw new Error('Expected deletion');
74	```

# Client API distinctions migration

[Documentation index](index.md) · [API reference](reference.md) · [Agent workflows](agent-workflows.md)

This breaking migration addresses the twenty findings from the 2026-10-31 review. Old spellings and ambiguous scalar rewrite outputs are removed. Keep host task meaning, retries, claims and durable acceptance outside CTT.

| Previous surface | Canonical surface |
| --- | --- |
| sortChildrenHints / ChildHintSorter / AsyncChildHintSorter | transformChildHints / ChildHintTransformer / AsyncChildHintTransformer |
| inspection hasSorter / hint frame stage sort | hasHintTransformer / transformHints |
| getChildrenHints() | getChildHints() |
| omittedWorkDependencies | dependsOnWorkDefault |
| configure({ limits }) | configure({ replaceLimits }) — constructors still accept limits |
| PreparedDag.vertices / PreparedDagVertex | liveVertexSummaries / PreparedDagVertexSummary |
| isTraversalLeaf | isChildExpansionSkipped — choose the query matching the intended meaning |
| createDagWorkSession / createAsyncDagWorkSession | bindDagWorkSession / bindAsyncDagWorkSession |
| outputAtReturn / getOutput() | outputResultAtReturn / getOutputResult() — tagged presence |
| discoveryCycle.vertexIds / DagDiscoveryCycleError.vertexIds | cycleWitnessVertexIds |
| structuralCycle.vertexIds | componentVertexIds |
| omitted result/slot vertexId presence | identity: { vertexId } or null |
| diagnostics.dependencies[].id / unmet | vertexId / unmetPrerequisiteIds |
| session inspect() generic details | DagWorkSessionControl with concrete DAG inspection |
| broad GraphWalkTarget / GraphWalkLink helpers | optional trailing hydration type parameter |
| edge-event/follow-context source | fromVertex — adapter source stays source |
| getVertexId / getPathsTo / getPathTo | requireVertexId / requirePathsTo / requirePathTo |
| explanation unknown / known | unresolved / live or omitted |
| instantiateDagFragment / DagFragmentInstance | mapDagFragmentIds returning DagFragment |
| public VertexRef | VertexHandle; mutable internal references have an explicit internal name |

## Hint ownership

Source content, standalone construction/clone patches and hint replacement commands accept readonly arrays. Vertex copies the membership array, including when cloned from another Vertex; editing the copy cannot change the original collection. Data and hint element objects retain shallow identity. Observed vertex collections remain frozen/detached. transformChildHints may invent, remove, duplicate or reorder hints; callers seeking sorting only should return a permutation themselves.

## Limits and sessions

replaceLimits replaces the entire previous limits record, rather than merging bounds. Include every bound you wish to retain; omitted/undefined replaceLimits retains the previous record. Validation is atomic, including route-mode bounds. Old limits patch keys reject even with own undefined. A constructor still takes limits.

Binding two sessions to one runner shares progress but does not share ticket authority. A ticket belongs to its issuing wrapper. Use preparedDag.createWorkSession() for independent progress; its topology is shared, not its work state. Keep settlement generations and tickets local.

## Presence and identity

outputResultAtReturn and getOutputResult() return `{ kind: 'present', value }` or `{ kind: 'absent' }`. Switch on kind before reading value. A present null or undefined remains present. Converters run only for present roots, receive the existing complete flag, and never interpret deletion. The captured result stays fixed; the final getter requires FINISHED and caches its first successful result. Existing failed conversion values propagate exactly and can be retried.

DAG omissions require explicit identity: null for anonymous, or `{ vertexId }` for known identity, including undefined/null/object/symbol IDs. During hint/prerequisite resolution, the requested identity can still supply an otherwise anonymous omission. Preserve satisfiesDependencies: true independently. Copy identity wrappers when converting records; never infer identity presence through truthiness. Structural result getters are supported; a known identity wrapper must contain an own vertexId. Raw top-level omitted.vertexId is rejected, and tree source results reject graph identity metadata.

Milestone explanations now discriminate unresolved, deleted, live and omitted. Live progress is non-null; omitted progress is null and its milestone is satisfied. A deferred/ready vertex is live, not completed. Diagnostic wait edges still mean waiter waits for prerequisite. Structural component lists are SCC membership, never consecutive cycle edges; discovery witnesses remain ordered and closed.

## Query and reconstruction choices

Use has()/nullable sibling queries to check absent handles. requireVertexId, requirePathsTo and requirePathTo intentionally throw for absence; null/undefined are valid IDs and cannot serve as failure sentinels. isChildExpansionSkipped reports an explicit DFS skip, not a structural leaf. Use hasNoChildHints for hint emptiness and the resolved child view for structural children, considering incomplete discovery.

liveVertexSummaries intentionally omits omission slots and entry metadata. Persist/revise/compose from definition, which preserves ordered slots, omissions and entry. mapDagFragmentIds maps caller identities explicitly; it does not issue a nominal instance capability. GraphWalkTarget and GraphWalkLink accept an optional trailing hydration mode to preserve mode-specific helper return types without assertions.

## Source and callback vocabulary

Only prerequisite lookup accepts `{ kind: 'missing' }`. All source resolutions use canonical tags; undefined and vertexContent:null legacy result forms are rejected. isArray/isObject are configuration predicates, while isComposite and getKeyPath are bound observations. Walking fromVertex identifies an endpoint; source config identifies the adapter. Callback timing, committed W/C observations, selector independence, resource disposal and package loader identity are unchanged.


## Tagged output example

<!-- standalone -->

```ts
import { rewriteObject } from 'configurable-tree-traversal';

const retained = rewriteObject(null).getOutputResult();
if (retained.kind !== 'present' || retained.value !== null) {
  throw new Error('Expected a present null document');
}
const deleted = rewriteObject({ task: 1 }, {
  rewrite: () => ({ kind: 'delete' }),
}).getOutputResult();
if (deleted.kind !== 'absent') throw new Error('Expected deletion');
```

1160	Rewrites run in post-order. Return `{ kind: 'rewrite', patch: { key, value } }` to rename or replace a property, `{ kind: 'delete' }` to remove it, or `undefined` / `{ kind: 'keep' }` for default assembly. Composite parents are reconstructed from their processed children. Arrays default to `arrayIndexPolicy: 'compactInTraversalOrder'`. Choose `'preserveNumericKeys'` to retain numeric positions and holes; output length is the larger of the original array length and highest assigned index plus one, preserving trailing holes and holes left by deletion. Non-arrays classified as arrays derive length from assigned indices. Numeric keys must be integers from 0 through 2^32-2. Named array properties remain supported. Built-in reconstruction defaults to `propertyCollision: 'error'`; `'firstWins'` and `'lastWins'` resolve duplicate normalized JavaScript property keys explicitly. Number/string equivalents collide, while distinct symbols retain identity. Custom `assembleArray`/`assembleObject` callbacks own placement and collision behavior for their respective composites. Null and undefined values are retained; deleting the root returns `null`.
1161	
1162	Set `assembleCompositesBeforeRewrite: true` to receive `assembledComposite` alongside the original property. Configurable classification options are `isArray` and `isObject`. Bound callback/binder observations include `isComposite`, `isArray`, `isObject`, and callback `getKeyPath({ noRoot: true })`; `isComposite` and `getKeyPath` are not configuration options. Custom `isArray`/`isObject` and `assembleArray`/`assembleObject` functions support specialized reconstruction. Default reconstruction is for plain objects and arrays; it does not preserve prototypes, descriptors, collection types, or identity shared between branches.
1163	
1164	`rewriteObject` retains its six generic positions, but default `Out` is now `unknown`: reconstruction and arbitrary rewrites cannot promise input shape/prototype preservation. A `convertRootValue(value: unknown, context: { readonly complete: boolean })` converter can infer its return type. A specific `Out` requires this converter, including when supplied through explicit generics or pretyped options. `complete` distinguishes the potentially partial initial snapshot from final output. The removed `getOutputObjectFromRootValue` option rejects. Use named root `rewriteObjectAs<Out>(input, options?)`, namespace `objectRewrite.rewriteObjectAs`, or the rewrite subpath helper for an explicit caller assertion; it performs no schema validation, and property values in its options remain unknown.
1165	
1166	`outputResultAtReturn` captures `ObjectRewriteOutputResult<Out>` when the helper returns, possibly partial while halted; it does not refresh on resume. Its variants are `{ kind: 'present', value: Out }` and `{ kind: 'absent' }`. A retained `null` or `undefined` root is present. Absent roots do not invoke `convertRootValue`. Resume through `result.traversalRunner.run()`, then call `result.getOutputResult()` for the final tagged result. The getter requires FINISHED and caches its first successful final conversion/result, reusing the initial result if the first run already finished. Exact conversion errors propagate without caching a success. Result wrappers are frozen; caller values remain shallow. The former scalar `outputAtReturn`/`getOutput()` APIs are removed.
1167	
1168	The helper owns its source. `traversableTree` is forbidden in inline and pretyped options; JavaScript presence, including present `undefined`, rejects before source, rewrite or conversion callbacks. Remove that field, or use a traversal directly for a custom source.
1169	
1170	`createObjectMutationBinder(options)` returns an `ObjectMutationBinder`; binding a vertex and context returns `ObjectMutationCommands`. Its `makeMutationCommand` builder consumes an `ObjectMutationRequest<Output>`. `ObjectMutationOptions` retains classifiers, assemblers, and `assembledMap`, keyed by reference identity. `ObjectCompositeClassification` names the bound array/object/composite flags. Generic stages are `TreeMutationCommandBinderFactory`, `TreeMutationCommandBinder`, `MutationCommands`, `MutationCommandBuilder`, `MutationRequest`, and `MutationCommand`.
1171	
1172	Generic `MutationCommandBuilder<Output, RewriteInput = Output['VertexData']>` uses `{ kind: 'rewrite', value }` for complete replacement data, `{ kind: 'delete' }` for deletion, and `{ kind: 'keep' }` for no mutation. Object helpers explicitly accept `ObjectPropertyPatch<Output>` (`Partial<Pick<Output['VertexData'], 'key' | 'value'>>`), so key-only and value-only patches remain typed. Omit the operation or return `{ kind: 'keep' }` for default assembly. Object rewrites use `{ kind: 'rewrite', patch }`; the patch must be a non-null object. Malformed or conflicting operations throw TypeError before assembly or mutation. `{ kind: 'rewrite', patch: { value: undefined } }` sets an undefined value when the output type permits it. User assembler errors propagate exactly. Unknown own patch fields, including non-enumerable string or symbol keys, throw TypeError. Existing payload metadata is retained; use `REWRITE_VERTEX_DATA` for full payload replacement.
1173	
1174	`ObjectRewriteCallback<InK, InV, OutK, OutV>` receives `ObjectRewriteInput` and `ObjectRewriteContext` with the same type parameters. Current keys and `getKeyPath()` include input and output keys. Current values are `unknown`: unchanged values and reconstructed containers can mix retained and replaced children, such as `[1, 'two']`. This applies to callback properties, vertex/ref/live tree, previous refs, classifiers, and assembler parent/child properties. `ObjectCurrentVertexTypes<InputTypes, OutputTypes>` preserves key identity and metadata alternatives without promising a narrow current value domain; narrowing by key or metadata cannot restore one. Assembler results, `assembledComposite`, and assembly cache values are also `unknown`. Requested replacement patches retain their declared `OutV` payload type. `originalTreeView` retains input types. `ObjectTreeVertexTypes<K, V>` names the object vertex-data/hint family; `ResolvedTreeVertexTypes<T>` names a tree whose data/hints are resolved vertex refs.
1175	
1176	Default `ObjectTreeSource` discovery exposes `PropertyKey`/`unknown`. Narrow key or value domains require both `getRootPropertyFromInputObject` and `getChildrenOfProperty`, including through `rewriteObject` options. `ObjectTreeSource.fromProperties(input, { getRootPropertyFromInputObject, getChildrenOfProperty })` provides a precise route with both adapters required and checked before input callbacks. Rewrites run in post-order. Return `{ kind: 'rewrite', patch: { key, value } }` to rename or replace a property, `{ kind: 'delete' }` to remove it, or `undefined` / `{ kind: 'keep' }` for default assembly. Composite parents are reconstructed from their processed children. Arrays default to `arrayIndexPolicy: 'compactInTraversalOrder'`. Choose `'preserveNumericKeys'` to retain numeric positions and holes; output length is the larger of the original array length and highest assigned index plus one, preserving trailing holes and holes left by deletion. Non-arrays classified as arrays derive length from assigned indices. Numeric keys must be integers from 0 through 2^32-2. Named array properties remain supported. Built-in reconstruction defaults to `propertyCollision: 'error'`; `'firstWins'` and `'lastWins'` resolve duplicate normalized JavaScript property keys explicitly. Number/string equivalents collide, while distinct symbols retain identity. Custom `assembleArray`/`assembleObject` callbacks own placement and collision behavior for their respective composites. Null and undefined values are retained; deleting the root returns `null`.

Set `assembleCompositesBeforeRewrite: true` to receive `assembledComposite` alongside the original property. Configurable classification options are `isArray` and `isObject`. Bound callback/binder observations include `isComposite`, `isArray`, `isObject`, and callback `getKeyPath({ noRoot: true })`; `isComposite` and `getKeyPath` are not configuration options. Custom `isArray`/`isObject` and `assembleArray`/`assembleObject` functions support specialized reconstruction. Default reconstruction is for plain objects and arrays; it does not preserve prototypes, descriptors, collection types, or identity shared between branches.

`rewriteObject` retains its six generic positions, but default `Out` is now `unknown`: reconstruction and arbitrary rewrites cannot promise input shape/prototype preservation. A `convertRootValue(value: unknown, context: { readonly complete: boolean })` converter can infer its return type. A specific `Out` requires this converter, including when supplied through explicit generics or pretyped options. `complete` distinguishes the potentially partial initial snapshot from final output. The removed `getOutputObjectFromRootValue` option rejects. Use named root `rewriteObjectAs<Out>(input, options?)`, namespace `objectRewrite.rewriteObjectAs`, or the rewrite subpath helper for an explicit caller assertion; it performs no schema validation, and property values in its options remain unknown.

`outputResultAtReturn` captures `ObjectRewriteOutputResult<Out>` when the helper returns, possibly partial while halted; it does not refresh on resume. Its variants are `{ kind: 'present', value: Out }` and `{ kind: 'absent' }`. A retained `null` or `undefined` root is present. Absent roots do not invoke `convertRootValue`. Resume through `result.traversalRunner.run()`, then call `result.getOutputResult()` for the final tagged result. The getter requires FINISHED and caches its first successful final conversion/result, reusing the initial result if the first run already finished. Exact conversion errors propagate without caching a success. Result wrappers are frozen; caller values remain shallow. The former scalar `outputAtReturn`/`getOutput()` APIs are removed.

The helper owns its source. `traversableTree` is forbidden in inline and pretyped options; JavaScript presence, including present `undefined`, rejects before source, rewrite or conversion callbacks. Remove that field, or use a traversal directly for a custom source.

`createObjectMutationBinder(options)` returns an `ObjectMutationBinder`; binding a vertex and context returns `ObjectMutationCommands`. Its `makeMutationCommand` builder consumes an `ObjectMutationRequest<Output>`. `ObjectMutationOptions` retains classifiers, assemblers, and `assembledMap`, keyed by reference identity. `ObjectCompositeClassification` names the bound array/object/composite flags. Generic stages are `TreeMutationCommandBinderFactory`, `TreeMutationCommandBinder`, `MutationCommands`, `MutationCommandBuilder`, `MutationRequest`, and `MutationCommand`.

Generic `MutationCommandBuilder<Output, RewriteInput = Output['VertexData']>` uses `{ kind: 'rewrite', value }` for complete replacement data, `{ kind: 'delete' }` for deletion, and `{ kind: 'keep' }` for no mutation. Object helpers explicitly accept `ObjectPropertyPatch<Output>` (`Partial<Pick<Output['VertexData'], 'key' | 'value'>>`), so key-only and value-only patches remain typed. Omit the operation or return `{ kind: 'keep' }` for default assembly. Object rewrites use `{ kind: 'rewrite', patch }`; the patch must be a non-null object. Malformed or conflicting operations throw TypeError before assembly or mutation. `{ kind: 'rewrite', patch: { value: undefined } }` sets an undefined value when the output type permits it. User assembler errors propagate exactly. Unknown own patch fields, including non-enumerable string or symbol keys, throw TypeError. Existing payload metadata is retained; use `REWRITE_VERTEX_DATA` for full payload replacement.

`ObjectRewriteCallback<InK, InV, OutK, OutV>` receives `ObjectRewriteInput` and `ObjectRewriteContext` with the same type parameters. Current keys and `getKeyPath()` include input and output keys. Current values are `unknown`: unchanged values and reconstructed containers can mix retained and replaced children, such as `[1, 'two']`. This applies to callback properties, vertex/ref/live tree, previous refs, classifiers, and assembler parent/child properties. `ObjectCurrentVertexTypes<InputTypes, OutputTypes>` preserves key identity and metadata alternatives without promising a narrow current value domain; narrowing by key or metadata cannot restore one. Assembler results, `assembledComposite`, and assembly cache values are also `unknown`. Requested replacement patches retain their declared `OutV` payload type. `originalTreeView` retains input types. `ObjectTreeVertexTypes<K, V>` names the object vertex-data/hint family; `ResolvedTreeVertexTypes<T>` names a tree whose data/hints are resolved vertex refs.

Default `ObjectTreeSource` discovery exposes `PropertyKey`/`unknown`. Narrow key or value domains require both `getRootPropertyFromInputObject` and `getChildrenOfProperty`, including through `rewriteObject` options. `ObjectTreeSource.fromProperties(input, { getRootPropertyFromInputObject, getChildrenOfProperty })` provides a precise route with both adapters required and checked before input callbacks. Explicit constructor generics cannot bypass these requirements.

`assembledMap` accepts `ObjectAssemblyCache<Key>`, a structural protocol with function-valued `has`, `get`, and `set` members. Its writer must accept `unknown`; a `Map<Key, unknown>` works, while `Map<Key, string>` rejects because mixed assembly would invalidate its reads. Cache keys retain reference identity.

DAG child relation data still uses its separate original `slotIndex`. Walking inspection exposes `executionOptions` and `activeVisitor.visitorIndex`.

## Values, original structure, object mutation, and tree positions

Use `MutableRef<T>.getValue()` / `.setValue(value)` in place of `CTTRef.unref()` / `.setPointsTo(value)`. `VertexRef<T>` is the exported vertex handle alias. `getRefId()` remains a reference UUID, distinct from arbitrary caller vertex IDs; retired `getId()` is removed. `GraphVertex`, `GraphVertexStatus`, and `GraphEdge` become `ResolvedGraphVertex`, `ResolvedVisitStage`, and `StructuralChildEdge`.

`VertexResolved` becomes `TreeVertexRecord` with `metadata` and `children`. These fields describe records and structural references; Vertex's canonical `$data` / `$childHints` remain distinct from structural references; retired aliases are removed. `ResolvedTree` becomes the standalone `ResolvedTreeStore`; ordinary runner queries use `getResolvedTreeView()` with restricted handles.

Replace `saveNotMutatedResolvedTree` / `saveNotMutatedResolvedGraph` with `retainOriginalTreeStructure` / `retainOriginalGraphStructure`, and context fields `notMutatedResolvedTree` / `notMutatedResolvedGraph` with `originalTreeView` / `originalGraphView`. The graph type is `OriginalGraphView`. Original-tree contexts expose `ResolvedTreeView` without storage mutators. Retention grows during discovery and shares payloads; it does not capture frozen deep data or a complete snapshot before discovery.

Replace `makeMutationCommandFactory` with `createObjectMutationBinder`. Its configured stage is `ObjectMutationBinder`, its bound stage `ObjectMutationCommands`, its patch `ObjectPropertyPatch`, and configuration `ObjectMutationOptions`. Classifier flags use `ObjectCompositeClassification`. Generic stages use `TreeMutationCommandBinderFactory`, `TreeMutationCommandBinder`, `MutationCommands`, `MutationCommandBuilder`, `MutationRequest`, and `MutationCommand`. Classifiers, custom assemblers, reference-keyed `assembledMap`, falsy values, symbol property keys, and patch-presence semantics are preserved.

The root `rewriteObject` export is now directly callable; use `objectRewrite` for the module namespace. Root/subpath callables retain identity under both CJS and ESM. `rewriteObjectAs` remains an assertion, and default output remains unknown.

Replace `DepthFirstTraversalInOrderTraversalConfig` / `inOrderTraversalConfig` with `InOrderOptions` / `inOrder`, and `IndexRange` with `ChildIndexSelection`. Fields become `afterChildIndices`, `fallbackChildIndices`, `visitSingleChildParent`, and `visitAfterOmittedChildren`. Index zero means after child slot zero; negative indices, range normalization, all-out-of-bounds fallback, and omitted-slot handling retain their behavior.

Use `Vertex.hasNoChildHints()`, runner `isTraversalLeaf(ref)`, and `hasSingleStructuralSink(graph)` for their separate hint, traversal, and structural-edge criteria. `filterDagDataVisitor` and `filterAsyncDagDataVisitor` predicate and visit payload data, retaining type-guard narrowing and async results.

| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Walking `followEdge`, `expandVertex`                                                       | `shouldFollowEdge`, `shouldExpandVertex`                                                   |
| `GraphWalkFollowEdge`, `AsyncGraphWalkFollowEdge`                                          | `GraphWalkEdgePredicate`, `AsyncGraphWalkEdgePredicate`                                    |
| `GraphWalkExpandVertex`, `AsyncGraphWalkExpandVertex`                                      | `GraphWalkExpansionPredicate`, `AsyncGraphWalkExpansionPredicate`                          |
| `filterDagVisitor`, `filterAsyncDagVisitor`                                                | `filterDagDataVisitor`, `filterAsyncDagDataVisitor`                                        |
| `Vertex.isLeafVertex`, runner `isLeafVertex`, `hasSingleSink`                              | `hasNoChildHints`, `isTraversalLeaf`, `hasSingleStructuralSink`                            |
| Walking `steps`, `maxSteps`                                                                | `candidateReadAttempts`, `maxCandidateReadAttempts`                                        |
| `occurrences`, `maxOccurrences`                                                            | `admittedTargets`, `maxAdmittedTargets`                                                    |
| Counts `foundVertices`, `omittedVertices`, `observedLinks`, `observations`                 | `uniqueFoundVertices`, `uniqueOmittedVertices`, `discoveredLinks`, `processedObservations` |
| Limit reasons `'maxSteps'`, `'maxOccurrences'`                                             | `'maxCandidateReadAttempts'`, `'maxAdmittedTargets'`; `'maxDepth'` is unchanged            |
| `DepthFirstTraversalInOrderTraversalConfig`, option `inOrderTraversalConfig`, `IndexRange` | `InOrderOptions`, option `inOrder`, `ChildIndexSelection`                                  |
| `visitParentAfterChildren`, `visitParentAfterChildrenAllRangesOutOfBoundsFallback`         | `afterChildIndices`, `fallbackChildIndices`                                                |
| `visitUpOneChildParents`, `considerVisitAfterNullContentVertices`                          | `visitSingleChildParent`, `visitAfterOmittedChildren`                                      |

Walking predicates make boolean decisions; `source.outgoing` discovers adjacency. DAG data filters pass payload data and preserve type-guard narrowing. `hasNoChildHints` inspects hints; `isTraversalLeaf` also considers disabled subtrees; `hasSingleStructuralSink` counts childless resolved vertices and ignores W/C edges.

Candidate read attempts include exhausted reads, duplicates and cached replay. Admissions include repeated/omitted targets. Fresh links count before follow predicates; cached replay does not rediscover them. Processed observations count acknowledged phase observations even when emission/callbacks are filtered. `maxDepth` still measures route edges; limits never measure callback time, tokens or unique emitted vertices.

In-order positions are child **indices**: zero means after child index zero. Negative indices and range normalization retain their rules. Fallback applies only when all configured ranges are out of bounds. Omitted-slot handling is independent of whether the child produced content; single-child parent handling remains separately configurable.

99	| Kind     | Fields                                                                                                                             |
100	| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
101	| `vertex` | `vertex`, route `depth`, incoming `via` edge or `null` for a root                                                                  |
102	| `edge`   | `edge`, found `fromVertex`, `depth` of the target route (source depth + 1), `target: { kind: 'found', vertex } \| { kind: 'omitted' }` |
103	| `path`   | Ordered `vertices`, ordered `edges`, route `depth`                                                                                 |
104	
105	In an edge record, `fromVertex` is the found source vertex; the constructor’s `source` is the adapter. Its `depth` describes the candidate target route even when that target is omitted. `GraphWalkEvent<Data, Edge, ID>` is that union. `GraphWalkEventFor<Data, Edge, Phase, ID>` and `GraphWalkPathEvent<Data, Edge, ID>` select precise records. Endpoint data stays typed; narrow `event.fromVertex.data.kind` and, after `event.target.kind === 'found'`, `event.target.vertex.data.kind` directly. No ID registry or fabricated tree `Vertex` is required. See the [typed reference example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/graph-walk-references-example.ts).
106	
107	A found root observes vertex then path. A followed link resolves/reuses its target, observes edge first, then vertex and path if a found occurrence is newly admitted under the policy. An omitted target of a followed link produces edge only. An omitted root has no incoming edge and produces no observation; it increments the `uniqueOmittedVertices` count and consumes a candidate read attempt and an admitted target. Record resolver outcomes in the host if omitted root IDs are needed. Under `once`, returning/self/parallel links still observe edges without repeated vertex/path observations. Visitor chains commit before their selected record emits. Expansion follows the occurrence's observations: a pause after yielding a vertex does not eagerly fetch adjacency. BFS preserves root/level source order; DFS exhausts each root's descendants before requesting the next root and follows outgoing order. Both are iterative. Pausing between edge and vertex retains pending observations and expansion without replaying resolution, completed callbacks or delivered records.
108	
109	`emitEvents` selects delivery; `visitorPhases` selects callbacks independently. Both use canonical field-wise selector patches, including empty selections and include/exclude filters; retired aliases reject. Hiding records/disabling callbacks changes neither discovery, budgets, nor revisit policy. An explicit call-level `emitEvents: [GraphWalkPhase.EDGE]` narrows every yield to edge records, including buffered records from an earlier lease. An omitted selector returns the broad union because persisted selectors can differ from defaults. Close the previous iterator before changing lease options. An admitted chain retains its callback configuration, while delivery uses the new lease's emission selection. Suppressed/delivered observations never replay; only pending observations before their delivery boundary can be newly selected. Tree and DAG iterators use the same delivery-time selection rule.
110	
111	Walking pending-request diagnostics use `operation: 'visit'` for callbacks in every walking phase. Source and iterator operations retain their distinct names, including `rootNext`, `edgeNext` and `iteratorReturn`.
112	
113	### Revisit policies, predicates, and bounds
114	
115	| `revisit`        | Vertex/path occurrences                              | Followed edges                                                      |
116	| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
117	| `once` (default) | One per found ID; path is its first-discovery prefix | Every followed link once, including back/self/parallel links        |
118	| `simplePaths`    | Each prefix without a repeated ID                    | Excludes a link closing a repeated vertex before `shouldFollowEdge` |
119	| `walks`          | Each prefix, including repeated IDs                  | Every eligible occurrence within bounds                             |
120	
121	Paths include zero-edge roots and every admitted prefix, not only leaves. Parallel links distinguish routes with identical vertex sequences. In route modes, a root reached from another root still contributes its own root path when declared; duplicate declarations of the same root do not. Source results/adjacency remain cached even when occurrences repeat. Use `once` for collecting reachable vertices and relationships; route enumeration can grow exponentially.
122	
123	`strategy: 'breadthFirst' | 'depthFirst'` chooses scheduling independently of revisit/emission. Depth counts route edges from zero. Under DFS/`once`, the first route fixes depth: finding a later shorter route does not re-expand a vertex. Use BFS for shortest discovery depth; DFS depth limits are not radius queries.
124	
125	`shouldFollowEdge(edge, context)` runs before target lookup; false prevents lookup through that occurrence. Context has found `fromVertex`, candidate target `depth`, and `revisit`; route policies add the current source-prefix `path`. The edge already identifies the relationship; context has no required `via`. `shouldExpandVertex(vertex, context)` runs after observations and before adjacency enumeration; context has occurrence `depth`, incoming `via`, `revisit`, and route `path` where applicable. False preserves observations while pruning expansion. Under `once`, the first expansion decision stands; route modes evaluate policy per prefix. The callback types are `GraphWalkEdgePredicate` and `GraphWalkExpansionPredicate`, with `Async` counterparts. Predicates must return booleans (promises allowed only for async). Commands do not control pruning.
126	
127	Limits are nonnegative safe integers, including zero. `simplePaths`/`walks` require `maxDepth` or `maxCandidateReadAttempts` at construction; `maxAdmittedTargets` alone is insufficient. Configuration patches validate merged options atomically and reject invalid transitions without mutation. A supplied `configure({ limits: ... })` record **replaces** the previous limits record; include each bound you want to retain. Runners snapshot options, selector arrays, visitor records and source callbacks/receiver; limits/topology policies are fixed for that runner. Larger bounds require a fresh runner. Unknown own option keys and unknown own limit keys reject with `TypeError` at construction or `configure()`, before discovery; invalid patches leave the previous configuration intact. Tree/DAG builders and public helper/option bags use the same strict own-key rule.

129	| Limit                      | Accounting and boundary                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

Explicit optional predicate/source undefined inputs remain valid under exact optional property typing. Fix the DAG configure source guard shipped in 0.11.0 to ignore inherited/own-undefined placeholders, capture source getters once, and retain atomic source-mode rejection.
7	- Clarify preparation/frontier choices, tree-only bases, legacy object adapter direct results, family root/slot distinctions, and buffered tree/DAG emission.

10	
11	- Simplify tree-source and object-hook omission to `{ kind: 'omitted' }`, including DAG traversal over tree adapters; reject graph acknowledgement metadata on trees while requiring explicit `satisfiesDependencies: true` on graph/prerequisite omissions.

## Unreleased

Explicit optional predicate/source undefined inputs remain valid under exact optional property typing. Fix the DAG configure source guard shipped in 0.11.0 to ignore inherited/own-undefined placeholders, capture source getters once, and retain atomic source-mode rejection.

- Unify expected preparation/composition/revision failures under `invalid.issues` and align collection dependency selectors with `dependsOn` / `dependsOnComplete`, rejecting retired selector keys. Clarify ticket dispatch, committed event timing, faithful definitions, walking adapter mapping and structural sink semantics in current guides.

- Simplify tree-source and object-hook omission to `{ kind: 'omitted' }`, including DAG traversal over tree adapters; reject graph acknowledgement metadata on trees while requiring explicit `satisfiesDependencies: true` on graph/prerequisite omissions.

- Expose shared lifecycle inspection and `inspectDag()` on sync/async coordination sessions; use `failTraversal` as the sole fatal settlement method.

161	Builders configure future runners; an existing runner retains its configuration snapshot. Sync and async variants use the same rules.
162	
163	| Field                                            | Omitted or `undefined` patch                                     | Defined patch                                                                                  |
164	| ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
165	| Walking `shouldFollowEdge`, `shouldExpandVertex` | Retain the previous predicate                                    | Callback replaces it; `null` clears it. Initial `null` also means absent.                      |
166	| Walking `replaceLimits`                          | Retain previous limits                                           | Replace the entire limits record; include every bound to retain.                               |
167	| `visitors` and `emitEvents` / `visitorPhases`    | Retain unspecified fields                                        | Patch visitor phases and selector fields independently, under their existing validation rules. |
168	| DAG `traversableTree` / `traversableGraph`       | Inherited keys and own `undefined` keys retain the active source | An own defined same-family source replaces it; an opposite-family source rejects.              |
169	
170	Every supported configure field accepts an explicit `undefined` under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`: missing and undefined fields retain prior values. This includes tree sources, concurrency, scheduling fields, each visitor phase, and each in-order field. `null` clears only explicitly nullable fields (walking predicates and `transformChildHints`). Walking constructors accept `limits`; configuration patches use `replaceLimits` to replace that record. A patch containing the former `limits` key rejects, including own `undefined`. Malformed defined fields reject atomically before registrations or configuration change; an existing runner keeps its snapshot. DAG construction requires exactly one own defined source and configure cannot change its source family. Source getters are captured once per request, without calling source callbacks.
171	
172	Public builders, helpers, mutation binders, execution options and nested option bags reject unsupported own string or symbol keys with `TypeError`, including non-enumerable keys and keys whose value is undefined. Source protocol objects can carry caller state and inherited methods; opaque data and IDs are not option bags. Path query options also reject unsupported own keys: `requirePathTo` / `requirePathsTo` accept only optional boolean `noRoot` and `noSelf` controls. Omitted or undefined controls use the default behavior, and accessors are captured once per query.
173	
174	## DAG traversal
175	
176	`DagTraversal` and `AsyncDagTraversal` traverse a discovered acyclic graph in two lifecycle orders: `ON_WORK_READY` visits eligible initial work, and `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` visits structural completion after the vertex’s work, discovery, and retained children complete. Under default `afterWorkReadyChain`, normal initial visitor-chain completion (including empty or filtered chains) satisfies work dependents; `externalSettlement` requires guarded host settlement; committed completion satisfies completion dependents. `dependsOnWork: [p]` waits for p's completed initial work (W); `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion: [p]` waits for p's committed `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` transition (C), including closed discovery and completion of every retained child. Both lists gate `ON_WORK_READY` conjunctively. Completion admission or an unfinished async completion callback does not satisfy C. Dependencies do not create structural parent/child edges; graph sources have no implicit parent W by default. Set `dependsOnWorkDefault: 'discoveryParentWork'` to inherit parent W when `dependsOnWork` is omitted; explicit lists, including `[]`, always win. Tree sources retain structural order and parent dependencies and reject explicit `rootWorkDependencies` or `dependsOnWorkDefault` options, including configuration patches. Graph source defaults are `rootWorkDependencies: 'honor'` and `dependsOnWorkDefault: 'none'`.

Every supported configure field accepts an explicit `undefined` under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`: missing and undefined fields retain prior values. This includes tree sources, concurrency, scheduling fields, each visitor phase, and each in-order field. `null` clears only explicitly nullable fields (walking predicates and `transformChildHints`). Walking constructors accept `limits`; configuration patches use `replaceLimits` to replace that record. A patch containing the former `limits` key rejects, including own `undefined`. Malformed defined fields reject atomically before registrations or configuration change; an existing runner keeps its snapshot. DAG construction requires exactly one own defined source and configure cannot change its source family. Source getters are captured once per request, without calling source callbacks.

Public builders, helpers, mutation binders, execution options and nested option bags reject unsupported own string or symbol keys with `TypeError`, including non-enumerable keys and keys whose value is undefined. Source protocol objects can carry caller state and inherited methods; opaque data and IDs are not option bags. Path query options also reject unsupported own keys: `requirePathTo` / `requirePathsTo` accept only optional boolean `noRoot` and `noSelf` controls. Omitted or undefined controls use the default behavior, and accessors are captured once per query.

## DAG traversal

`DagTraversal` and `AsyncDagTraversal` traverse a discovered acyclic graph in two lifecycle orders: `ON_WORK_READY` visits eligible initial work, and `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` visits structural completion after the vertex’s work, discovery, and retained children complete. Under default `afterWorkReadyChain`, normal initial visitor-chain completion (including empty or filtered chains) satisfies work dependents; `externalSettlement` requires guarded host settlement; committed completion satisfies completion dependents. `dependsOnWork: [p]` waits for p's completed initial work (W); `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion: [p]` waits for p's committed `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` transition (C), including closed discovery and completion of every retained child. Both lists gate `ON_WORK_READY` conjunctively. Completion admission or an unfinished async completion callback does not satisfy C. Dependencies do not create structural parent/child edges; graph sources have no implicit parent W by default. Set `dependsOnWorkDefault: 'discoveryParentWork'` to inherit parent W when `dependsOnWork` is omitted; explicit lists, including `[]`, always win. Tree sources retain structural order and parent dependencies and reject explicit `rootWorkDependencies` or `dependsOnWorkDefault` options, including configuration patches. Graph source defaults are `rootWorkDependencies: 'honor'` and `dependsOnWorkDefault: 'none'`.

205	Use synchronous `runner.inspectMilestones()` (also on async runners), or the equivalent `inspectDagMilestones(runner)`, when a host needs to show why a milestone is blocked or which original constraints depend on it. Capture once, then call `explain({ vertexId, milestone: 'work' | 'subgraphCompletion' })`, `prerequisitesOf(...)`, or `dependentsOf(..., { transitive: true })`. Explanations distinguish unknown/deleted identities, omitted vertices, unfinished work, incomplete local discovery and pending completion transitions. A ready or externally deferred task still has unfinished W; a seeded parent's W may be satisfied while its C waits for children. Constraint endpoints include work state and milestone satisfaction, without interpreting business outcomes.

207	Inspect after `prepare()` for an eager validated view, or during lazy traversal for partial facts. `discoveryComplete: false` limits the captured domain, and an unresolved endpoint is not a proven missing task. Captures stay unchanged after settlement; capture again to refresh. These queries perform no callbacks, lookup, scheduling, or ownership changes, including while an iterator or pending async callback owns the runner. Static navigation keeps original constraints after milestones complete; explanations stop at satisfied milestones. See the [query contract](reference.md#dag-dependency-queries-and-explanations) and [runnable inspection example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-inspection-example.ts).

Inspection reports callback `phase` separately from chain `state`, `visitorIndex`, and admitted `executionOptions`; pending requests name their public callback `operation`. Graph `visitStage` records scheduling boundaries and cannot establish active callbacks or host-agent progress; deferred work may remain `INITIAL_VISIT_STARTED` after callbacks drain. Both are observational; neither drives traversal. See [progress contracts](reference.md#deferred-dag-progress-and-reconciliation) and [inspection](reference.md#inspection-and-execution) for exact fields and limits.

**Result: no source-level blockers. All twenty requirements are implemented in the working tree with regression evidence. One packaged-guide sentence still advertises the retired `configure({ limits })` form and should be corrected before merge.**

## Findings

**Important (verified defect, documentation contract)**

1. **Reference guide still advertises the rejected limits patch.** `docs/reference.md:127` says a supplied `configure({ limits: ... })` record replaces the previous limits record. The runtime rejects that key: `src/traversals/graph-walk/lib/normalizeWalkOptions.ts:156-167` switches the accepted key to `replaceLimits` whenever a previous configuration exists, and `assertOwnKeys` throws `TypeError: Unknown option: limits`. The same file contradicts itself three paragraphs later at line 170. Trigger: a reader copies the line-127 form into a builder patch and gets a TypeError, which is exactly the R04 class of defect. Fix: change line 127 to `configure({ replaceLimits: ... })` and drop the bold "replaces" claim about `limits`.

**Minor (verified, documentation wording)**

2. **Older packaged migration guides present retired names as current.** `docs/migration-uniform-api.md:370` states that `VertexRef<T>` is the exported handle alias, and line 382 plus `docs/migration-api-clarity.md:211,220` name `isTraversalLeaf` as canonical. Both guides carry a banner at line 3 pointing to the new migration, so impact is low. Fix: mark those sentences as superseded or substitute `VertexHandle` and `isChildExpansionSkipped`.
3. **Workflow guide uses the retired explanation literal.** `docs/agent-workflows.md:205` says explanations distinguish "unknown/deleted identities". The public literal is now `unresolved` (`src/traversals/dag-traversal/lib/DagInspection.ts:48`). Fix: say "unresolved/deleted".
4. **Audit record overstates walking wrapper freezing.** `requirements.json` R16 says "frozen detached wrappers". Edge events and follow contexts are detached plain copies, not frozen (`src/traversals/graph-walk/lib/WalkKernel.ts:242-248, 298-303`), and `tests/graph-walk-observations.test.ts:196-197` deliberately mutates them. The design spec and reference only promise detachment, so this is a record-wording issue, not a code defect. Fix: reword the requirement to "detached".
5. **No changelog entry.** `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased has no line for this breaking migration. The design did not require one, so this is a preference.

**Preferences (not defects)**

- Private engine names `sortHints` and `SORT_HINTS` remain in `src/core/drivers/callbackBindings.ts:158` and `src/core/TraversalKernel.ts:666`. They are mapped to the public `transformChildHints` operation and never surface. Optional cleanup.

## Findings

**Important (verified defect, documentation contract)**

1. **Reference guide still advertises the rejected limits patch.** `docs/reference.md:127` says a supplied `configure({ limits: ... })` record replaces the previous limits record. The runtime rejects that key: `src/traversals/graph-walk/lib/normalizeWalkOptions.ts:156-167` switches the accepted key to `replaceLimits` whenever a previous configuration exists, and `assertOwnKeys` throws `TypeError: Unknown option: limits`. The same file contradicts itself three paragraphs later at line 170. Trigger: a reader copies the line-127 form into a builder patch and gets a TypeError, which is exactly the R04 class of defect. Fix: change line 127 to `configure({ replaceLimits: ... })` and drop the bold "replaces" claim about `limits`.

**Minor (verified, documentation wording)**

2. **Older packaged migration guides present retired names as current.** `docs/migration-uniform-api.md:370` states that `VertexRef<T>` is the exported handle alias, and line 382 plus `docs/migration-api-clarity.md:211,220` name `isTraversalLeaf` as canonical. Both guides carry a banner at line 3 pointing to the new migration, so impact is low. Fix: mark those sentences as superseded or substitute `VertexHandle` and `isChildExpansionSkipped`.
3. **Workflow guide uses the retired explanation literal.** `docs/agent-workflows.md:205` says explanations distinguish "unknown/deleted identities". The public literal is now `unresolved` (`src/traversals/dag-traversal/lib/DagInspection.ts:48`). Fix: say "unresolved/deleted".
4. **Audit record overstates walking wrapper freezing.** `requirements.json` R16 says "frozen detached wrappers". Edge events and follow contexts are detached plain copies, not frozen (`src/traversals/graph-walk/lib/WalkKernel.ts:242-248, 298-303`), and `tests/graph-walk-observations.test.ts:196-197` deliberately mutates them. The design spec and reference only promise detachment, so this is a record-wording issue, not a code defect. Fix: reword the requirement to "detached".
5. **No changelog entry.** `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased has no line for this breaking migration. The design did not require one, so this is a preference.

**Preferences (not defects)**

- Private engine names `sortHints` and `SORT_HINTS` remain in `src/core/drivers/callbackBindings.ts:158` and `src/core/TraversalKernel.ts:666`. They are mapped to the public `transformChildHints` operation and never surface. Optional cleanup.
